nodes.question: Which surface is 'the Today button'? No control named Today was found. Candidates: the 'All subjects' row with its Today column in the Mac review subjects view, an iOS equivalent in review-subjects-screen.swift, or the Expo 'Today' screen. I did not read review-subjects-screen.swift or the web app.
nodes.quote: The Today button groups today's cards by subject
nodes.answer: The iOS review-subjects screen has an 'All subjects' row. Tapping it selects scope 'all'. Its start control is a main-action tile titled 'Start review', or 'Start review: <name>' when a subject is selected. Nothing on this screen is labelled 'Today'. On the iOS review-subjects screen, starting with 'all' or no selection sets reviewsAll and opens session(nil, learnAhead.days). Starting with a subject routes to DueReviewScope(subject:). The Mac subject row header has a literal 'Today' column title, which is a count column, not a button. The only 'Today' control that starts a review is the iOS DueTodayRow. It reads 'Due today', shows a total and a review/learning/new breakdown, and is a NavigationLink to DueReviewScreen. It appears on HomeScreen and on TodayScreen. TodayScreen (navigation title 'Today') contains the DueTodayRow section. It is reached from the More screen via the .today destination. The Mac app has a 'Today' feature entry and MacHomeView is titled 'Today'. It holds a DueTodayModel. The web sidebar has no control named Today. Its only 'Today' match is the newRemainingToday count. The web app has Today count columns for subjects in subject-today-columns.tsx and knowledge-browser-subject-list.tsx. The Expo mobile app's index screen is titled 'Today'. It shows a single probe-push question with no subject grouping, so it is not a card-review surface. Subject grouping, the current-subject label and the next-subject announcement ('Next subject: <path> · N cards here, M cards left in total') already exist in the iOS shared review code, which is the path DueReviewScreen uses. The 'Today' surfaces that start a review (DueTodayRow, the All-subjects start) feed this path. Rule r1 applies only if the work touches apps/mobile (Expo): read the Expo v57 docs first.

nodes.question: Grouping, the current-subject label and the next-subject announcement already exist in the API and the iOS DueReviewModel. Should the work cover only the missing surface (Mac, web or Expo), or re-verify and change the existing iOS behaviour? I did not check whether the Today/all-subjects scope reaches this grouped path.
nodes.quote: shows the current subject, and announces the next subject with how many cards remain
nodes.answer: The API review-cards handler passes tag, topic, card and subject filters to the queue (all optional), then always runs groupReviewCardsBySubject over the result. Grouping therefore applies to every scope, including an unscoped request. groupReviewCardsBySubject orders cards by the first appearance of each subjectId, keeps the original order within a group, and attaches a subjectPath label (null when there is no label). iOS Today entry: DueTodayCard opens DueReviewScreen() with no scope. DueReviewModel.load then sends subjectId: scope?.subjectId, which is nil, to the API. So in the online path the all-subjects Today scope does reach the grouped endpoint. DueReviewModel.load calls APIClient.reviewCards and then queues the cards in server order, with no re-sorting on the client. The iOS model already exposes currentSubjectPath (the current-subject label) and groupAnnouncement. The announcement shows only when the subject changes and the card is not revealed. It uses the cards left in the group plus the overall remaining count. ReviewSubjectGroups builds the announcement text 'Next subject: <path> · N cards here, M cards left in total'. cardsLeft counts the current card plus the following queue cards with the same path. DueReviewCardBody renders the announcement, and DueReviewModel records previousSubjectPath when it moves to the next card. Tests exist for the API grouping and for the iOS announcement text, and the iOS ReviewCard decoder has a subjectPath test. The web client's review API file references only a subjectId query key. It has no subjectPath, grouping or announcement code, so web has none of the surface. The Mac app uses DueReviewModel (MacDueReviewView, MacDecideView). It shares the Shared model, so the label and announcement logic is available there. Whether Mac renders them was not verified. The mobile app has an AGENTS.md carrying the rule to read the versioned Expo docs before writing code. It is the only mobile file found that touches this feature. A mobile review screen using this endpoint was not found.

nodes.question: Does 'how many cards remain' mean cards left in the next subject's group, cards left overall, or both? The iOS announcement currently gives both.

The grouping order is the order subjects first appear in the queue. Should it stay that way, or be ordered some other way (for example alphabetical or by due count), and how should it interact with the planned Shuffle option?
